Independent editorial policy · updated 7 October 2026

Editorial standards & research method

How this independent research site evaluates public information about the LoloBuy shopping workflow.

Who publishes this site: “LoloBuy AT Research” is the editorial label used by this independent research resource. It is not LoloBuy, a marketplace seller, a carrier or a customs authority, and it does not accept payments or place orders for visitors.

What we publish

Our guides are written to help a buyer check a concrete decision: a selected product option, warehouse evidence, parcel weight, route information, tracking event or after-sales step. They are not promises about price, authenticity, customs clearance, delivery dates or the outcome of an individual order.

How evidence is handled

We distinguish between three kinds of material: public service documentation, dated public reviews or app-listing observations, and buyer-preparation advice. A published policy explains what a service says it offers. A public review describes one person’s report. Neither is treated as a guarantee that the same result will apply to every seller, parcel, country or date.

Where a fact can change—such as a fee, route, payment method, service window or availability—we avoid presenting a universal figure. The guide instead identifies the live screen or account record a buyer should verify before paying.

How reviews are evaluated

Review articles state the date of the snapshot, the source types consulted and important limitations such as a small sample, an invitation label, a referral link or an incomplete outcome. We give more weight to a report that identifies the relevant order stage and evidence than to a bare star rating or a broad claim without transaction detail.

Updates and corrections

Each guide shows a checked or reviewed date near its title. We update that date only when the page receives a substantive factual, methodological or explanatory change. If a public source changes, conflicts with the page or proves inaccurate, we revise or remove the affected statement rather than preserving it for search visibility.

What readers should do

Use these pages as a preparation checklist, then rely on the current order, warehouse, parcel, carrier or official service record for a live transaction. Preserve your own product link, selected variant, QC evidence, payment record and tracking details; those records are more relevant to your order than a general guide.

Independent research resource · Editorial standards are published for readers, not as an affiliation claim.
